recordings.text: Natural boundaries such as mountains, lakes, and rivers determine the shapes and sizes of many eastern states. Locate the map on pp. 346–347 in the student text NWHG and identify these rivers and lakes that serve as parts of state boundaries:
The states along the Atlantic Coast owe much to the Atlantic Ocean. America’s first great states grew by its bays and harbors. Locate Massachusetts Bay, Chesapeake Bay, and Long Island Sound.

Between Lake Erie and Lake Ontario, the waters of the Niagara River flow over a cliff in a cascade that is one of North America’s great natural wonders—Niagara Falls. Look between the two lakes to find Niagara Falls.

Down the center of Florida runs a long chain of lakes which ends with Lake Okeechobee, one of the largest freshwater lakes within a state. The waters of Lake Okeechobee drain southward through marshes and savannas for 120 miles to the Atlantic, forming the Everglades. Can you locate the Everglades?
Look for the Okefenokee Swamp in Georgia near the Florida border. Like the Everglades, it has become a wildlife preserve.

Look along the coast of North Carolina. The long barrier islands you see there are called the Outer Banks. These sandy reefs form Cape Hatteras and Cape Lookout. Another cape, Cape Fear, is called the “graveyard of the Atlantic” because its shifting sands have caused so many shipwrecks.
New England States. Maine. New Hampshire. Vermont. Massachusetts. Connecticut. Rhode Island
Middle Atlantic States. Delaware. Maryland. New Jersey. New York. Pennsylvania
Southeastern States. West Virginia. Virginia. Kentucky. Tennessee. North Carolina. South Carolina. Georgia. Alabama. Florida
Natural boundary features. Chattahoochee R.. Connecticut R.. Savannah R.. Delaware R.. Lake Champlain. Ohio R.. Lake Ontario. Mississippi R.. Lake Erie
1. Which two states are separated in part by the Chattahoochee River?. A. New York and Vermont. B. Vermont and New Hampshire. C. Ohio and Kentucky. D. Alabama and Georgia
2. Which river forms part of the boundary between Vermont and New Hampshire?. A. Savannah River. B. Mississippi River. C. Chattahoochee River. D. Connecticut River
3. Which river forms part of the boundary between Georgia and South Carolina?. A. Connecticut River. B. Ohio River. C. Delaware River. D. Savannah River
4. Which river forms part of the boundary between Pennsylvania and New Jersey?. A. Mississippi River. B. Delaware River. C. Savannah River. D. Chattahoochee River
5. Which lake lies along part of the boundary between New York and Vermont?. A. Lake Champlain. B. Lake Michigan. C. Lake Superior. D. Lake Okeechobee
6. Which river forms part of the boundary between Ohio and Kentucky?. A. Delaware River. B. Connecticut River. C. Savannah River. D. Ohio River
7. Which state borders Lake Ontario?. A. Alabama. B. Florida. C. New York. D. Georgia
8. Which river separates Tennessee and Arkansas along part of their boundary?. A. Connecticut River. B. Chattahoochee River. C. Mississippi River. D. Delaware River
9. Which of these states borders Lake Erie?. A. Maine. B. Georgia. C. Florida. D. Ohio
10. Which state is beside Massachusetts Bay?. A. Georgia. B. Maryland. C. Massachusetts. D. Florida
11. Which two states border Chesapeake Bay?. A. New York and Vermont. B. Virginia and Maryland. C. Maine and New Hampshire. D. Georgia and Alabama
12. Long Island Sound is between which two states?. A. Georgia and Florida. B. Ohio and Kentucky. C. New York and Connecticut. D. Maine and Vermont
13. The Chesapeake Bay cuts into what states?. A. Maine and New Hampshire. B. Virginia and Maryland. C. Georgia and Alabama. D. New York and Vermont
14. What southeastern state is one big peninsula nearly surrounded by ocean water?. A. Tennessee. B. Florida. C. Kentucky. D. West Virginia
15. Which New England state is landlocked with no direct access to the ocean?. A. Rhode Island. B. Massachusetts. C. Maine. D. Vermont

16. Between which two lakes does the Niagara River form Niagara Falls?. A. Lake Erie and Lake Ontario. B. Lake Champlain and Lake Okeechobee. C. Lake Huron and Lake Superior. D. Lake Superior and Lake Michigan
17. Which lake’s waters drain southward through marshes and savannas to form the Everglades?. A. Lake Okeechobee. B. Lake Ontario. C. Lake Erie. D. Lake Champlain
18. In which state does this worksheet locate the Okefenokee Swamp near the Florida border?. A. Kentucky. B. New York. C. Maine. D. Georgia
19. Which state has the barrier islands called the Outer Banks?. A. Maryland. B. North Carolina. C. Vermont. D. Connecticut

20. What cape in Florida is the site of the Kennedy Space Center? What well-known Massachusetts cape juts out into the Atlantic Ocean?. A. Cape Cod; Cape Canaveral. B. Cape Fear; Cape Hatteras. C. Cape Hatteras; Cape Lookout. D. Cape Canaveral; Cape Cod

Missouri; Iowa; Minnesota; Kansas; Nebraska; North Dakota; South Dakota; Oklahoma; Texas
Arkansas; Louisiana; Mississippi

In general, the area between the Appalachian Mountains and the Rocky Mountains consists of either flat plains or gently rolling hills. There are a few low mountain ranges, however. Locate the map on pp. 346–347 in the student text NWHG. In what states do you find the Black Hills? Ozark Mountains? Mesabi Range? Can you find the Great Plains?

America is unusual because her midwest, though far from the sea, is still heavily populated. Business in the Midwest flourishes because of two routes to the sea: the St. Lawrence Seaway and the Mississippi River.

Find the Straits of Mackinac, an important link in the water route between Lake Michigan and the Atlantic Ocean. The straits connect Lake Michigan and Lake Huron at the northern end of the Lower Peninsula of Michigan.
1. In what state do you find the Black Hills?. A. South Dakota. B. Iowa. C. Louisiana
2. Which of these states has the Ozark Mountains?. A. Wisconsin. B. Missouri. C. North Dakota
3. In what state do you find the Mesabi Range?. A. Oklahoma. B. Kansas. C. Minnesota

4. Which location describes the Great Plains?. A. West of the Mississippi River and east of the Rocky Mountains. B. Along the Atlantic Coast in New England. C. Entirely within the Appalachian Mountains
5. In what state does the Mississippi River begin?. A. Missouri. B. Minnesota. C. Louisiana
6. What great eastern river joins the Mississippi in southern Illinois?. A. Ohio River. B. Columbia River. C. Rio Grande
7. What great western river flows through Omaha, Nebraska, and joins the Mississippi in eastern Missouri?. A. Colorado River. B. Hudson River. C. Missouri River
8. In what state does the Mississippi River finish its course?. A. Louisiana. B. Illinois. C. Minnesota
9. Which pair of states borders the Mississippi River?. A. Ohio and Indiana. B. Minnesota and Wisconsin. C. Kansas and Nebraska
10. Which pair of states borders the Mississippi River?. A. Oklahoma and Texas. B. Iowa and Illinois. C. Michigan and Ohio
11. Which pair of states borders the Mississippi River?. A. Missouri and Kentucky. B. North Dakota and South Dakota. C. Kansas and Oklahoma
12. Which pair of states borders the Mississippi River?. A. Tennessee and Arkansas. B. Nebraska and Kansas. C. Texas and Oklahoma
13. Which pair of states borders the Mississippi River?. A. Alabama and Florida. B. Mississippi and Louisiana. C. Georgia and South Carolina
14. Which states border Lake Superior?. A. New York, Pennsylvania, Ohio. B. Ohio, Indiana, Illinois. C. Minnesota, Wisconsin, Michigan
15. Which states border Lake Michigan?. A. Iowa, Missouri, Kentucky, Tennessee. B. Wisconsin, Illinois, Indiana, Michigan. C. Minnesota, Ohio, Pennsylvania, New York
16. Which state borders Lake Huron?. A. Ohio. B. Michigan. C. Wisconsin
17. Which states border Lake Erie?. A. Iowa, Missouri, Kentucky, Tennessee. B. Wisconsin, Illinois, Indiana, Minnesota. C. Michigan, Ohio, Pennsylvania, New York
18. Which state borders Lake Ontario?. A. New York. B. Michigan. C. Ohio

19. Which names identify the five Great Lakes?. A. Champlain, Okeechobee, Itasca, Crater, and Tahoe. B. Great Salt Lake, Titicaca, Maracaibo, Winnipeg, and Nicaragua. C. Superior, Michigan, Huron, Erie, and Ontario
20. Which of the Great Lakes is entirely within the boundaries of the United States?. A. Lake Huron. B. Lake Ontario. C. Lake Michigan
21. Which two lakes do the Straits of Mackinac connect?. A. Lake Erie and Lake Ontario. B. Lake Superior and Lake Erie. C. Lake Michigan and Lake Huron
22. Which rivers form the boundaries of the Great Lakes States?. A. Hudson, Delaware, and Potomac rivers. B. Colorado, Columbia, and Snake rivers. C. Mississippi, Ohio, and Wabash rivers
23. What North Central State is made up of two peninsulas surrounded by fresh water?. A. Michigan. B. Ohio. C. Wisconsin
24. The state of Iowa sits between what two rivers?. A. Colorado and Rio Grande rivers. B. Missouri and Mississippi rivers. C. Ohio and Wabash rivers
25. What South Central States border the Gulf of Mexico?. A. Mississippi and Louisiana. B. Arkansas and Oklahoma. C. Kansas and Nebraska
26. List two central states that have panhandles.. A. Wisconsin and Minnesota. B. Iowa and Missouri. C. Texas and Oklahoma
27. What city lies at the junction of the Ohio and Mississippi Rivers?. A. Cairo, Illinois. B. Chicago, Illinois. C. Duluth, Minnesota
28. What city lies just south of the junction of the Missouri and Mississippi Rivers?. A. Omaha, Nebraska. B. St. Louis, Missouri. C. Cincinnati, Ohio

29. Find the large Texas city that, though 50 miles from the Gulf of Mexico, is one of America’s greatest ports, thanks to a man-made channel. It’s also the location of NASA’s Mission Control.. A. Houston, Texas. B. Austin, Texas. C. Dallas, Texas
30. On which body of water is Chicago located?. A. Lake Superior. B. Lake Erie. C. Lake Michigan
31. On which body of water is Cincinnati located?. A. Missouri River. B. Mississippi River. C. Ohio River
32. On which body of water is Milwaukee located?. A. Lake Erie. B. Lake Michigan. C. Lake Huron
33. On which body of water is Toledo located?. A. Lake Superior. B. Lake Erie. C. Lake Ontario
34. On which body of water is New Orleans located?. A. Lake Superior. B. Gulf of Mexico. C. Lake Erie
35. On which body of water is Omaha located?. A. Mississippi River. B. Ohio River. C. Missouri River
36. On which body of water is Duluth located?. A. Lake Superior. B. Lake Ontario. C. Lake Michigan

Many rivers have their headwaters in the Rocky Mountains, some of which flow east across the plains and some of which flow west toward the Pacific Ocean. Locate the map on pp. 346–347 in the student text NWHG. Find the following rivers on the map and trace their routes from their beginnings in the Rockies to their destinations east or west.
The West is known for its rugged mountains. The majestic chain of the Rocky Mountains is called the “Roof of America.” Farther west are two other mountain chains.

Between the western mountains are plateaus, valleys, and a vast arid region called the North American Desert. This desert covers parts of eleven western states and is divided into five regions. Study the map and locate the five regions.
1. The river that begins in Colorado and flows through the city of Pueblo before joining the Mississippi River.. A. Colorado River. B. Arkansas River. C. Columbia River

2. The river that begins in Colorado and flows south through New Mexico and along the border between Texas and Mexico before emptying into the Gulf of Mexico.. A. Rio Grande. B. Snake River. C. Ohio River
3. The river that runs through the Grand Canyon and forms the boundary between California and Arizona.. A. Missouri River. B. Columbia River. C. Colorado River
4. The river that begins in the northern Rockies and flows along the border between Washington and Oregon to the Pacific.. A. Columbia River. B. Arkansas River. C. Rio Grande

5. The river that begins in the northern Rockies and flows through Montana and the Dakotas and across the Midwest until it joins the Mississippi River north of St. Louis.. A. Snake River. B. Colorado River. C. Missouri River
6. The river that flows across Idaho, forming part of Idaho’s western border before joining the Columbia River.. A. Snake River. B. Ohio River. C. Hudson River
7. What chain rises from the Pacific Ocean along the coasts of California and Oregon?. A. Coastal Ranges. B. Appalachians. C. Ozarks
8. Mt. McKinley, North America’s tallest peak, is in what state?. A. California. B. Colorado. C. Alaska
9. Look in western Oregon and Washington for the great range of rugged mountains which includes Mt. Rainier, Mt. Shasta, and Mt. St. Helens.. A. Black Hills. B. Ozarks. C. Cascade Range

10. Look in eastern California for the mountain range known for its forests of giant sequoias and for having North America’s tallest peak south of Alaska. What is the range? What is the peak?. A. Sierra Nevada; Mount Whitney. B. Rocky Mountains; Mount Elbert. C. Cascade Range; Mount Rainier

11. Which list names the five regions of the North American Desert in this lesson?. A. Great Basin, Colorado Plateau, Mojave, Sonoran, and Chihuahuan. B. Great Plains, Ozarks, Appalachians, Cascades, and Sierras. C. Sahara, Gobi, Kalahari, Namib, and Thar
12. What lake in the Great Basin Desert is the largest saltwater lake in North America? In what state is it located?. A. Lake Tahoe; Nevada. B. Crater Lake; Oregon. C. Great Salt Lake; Utah

13. In California, between the Coastal Ranges and the Sierra Nevada Range lies the Central Valley. A break in the Coastal Ranges makes an entrance to the valley from the coast. This break is called the Golden Gate. What city is located here? Hint: a beautiful suspension bridge crosses the entrance.. A. San Diego. B. San Francisco. C. Los Angeles

14. The Atlantic Coast has many natural harbors and bays. The Pacific Coast, however, has cliffs and rocky shores. (One of the few natural harbors is San Francisco Bay.) One very busy port is man-made. The city that has grown around it is now California’s largest. Can you find this southern California city?. A. Los Angeles. B. San Francisco. C. Sacramento

15. Sail through the Juan de Fuca Strait which lies between Canada’s Vancouver Island and Washington State. Go south and enter Puget Sound to get to Washington’s busy industrial area. What beautiful port city will you reach?. A. San Francisco. B. Portland. C. Seattle

The Appalachian Mountains, North America’s second largest mountain system, extend from Canada to Alabama and are made up of many mountain ranges. Using the map on p. 50 of your textbook, find the states most associated with the following ranges of the Appalachian Mountains:
Using the map on pp. 346–347 of your textbook, locate these port cities and name their states and the bodies of water on which they are located.
Which eastern capital city is on the Connecticut River? The Susquehanna River? The Atlantic Coast?
What is the capital city of America’s smallest state and the name of that state?
1. Which state or states does the worksheet associate with the Green Mountains?. A. New Hampshire. B. North Carolina. C. Vermont. D. Tennessee and North Carolina
2. Which state or states does the worksheet associate with the White Mountains?. A. Vermont. B. New York. C. New Hampshire. D. North Carolina
3. Which state or states does the worksheet associate with the Catskill Mountains?. A. New York. B. Tennessee and Alabama. C. Tennessee and North Carolina. D. North Carolina
4. Which state or states does the worksheet associate with the Allegheny Mountains?. A. New Hampshire. B. Tennessee and North Carolina. C. Vermont. D. Pennsylvania
5. Which state or states does the worksheet associate with the Blue Ridge Mountains?. A. Vermont. B. Tennessee and Alabama. C. Tennessee and North Carolina. D. North Carolina
6. Which state or states does the worksheet associate with the Great Smoky Mountains?. A. North Carolina. B. Tennessee and North Carolina. C. Tennessee and Alabama. D. Vermont
7. Which state or states does the worksheet associate with the Cumberland Mountains?. A. Tennessee and Alabama. B. Tennessee and North Carolina. C. Vermont. D. New Hampshire
8. In which state is Portland, and on which body of water is it located?. A. New York; Lake Erie. B. Maine; Atlantic Ocean. C. Massachusetts; Massachusetts Bay. D. Maryland; Chesapeake Bay
9. In which state is Boston, and on which body of water is it located?. A. Massachusetts; Massachusetts Bay. B. Alabama; Gulf of Mexico. C. Maine; Atlantic Ocean. D. Virginia; Chesapeake Bay
10. In which state is Buffalo, and on which body of water is it located?. A. South Carolina; Atlantic Ocean. B. New York; Lake Erie. C. Virginia; Chesapeake Bay. D. Maryland; Chesapeake Bay

11. In which state is Baltimore, and on which body of water is it located?. A. South Carolina; Atlantic Ocean. B. Maryland; Chesapeake Bay. C. Massachusetts; Massachusetts Bay. D. Virginia; Chesapeake Bay
12. In which state is Norfolk, and on which body of water is it located?. A. Alabama; Gulf of Mexico. B. Virginia; Chesapeake Bay. C. Maine; Atlantic Ocean. D. New York; Lake Erie
13. In which state is Charleston, and on which body of water is it located?. A. New York; Lake Erie. B. Maryland; Chesapeake Bay. C. South Carolina; Atlantic Ocean. D. Virginia; Chesapeake Bay
14. In which state is Mobile, and on which body of water is it located?. A. Massachusetts; Massachusetts Bay. B. Virginia; Chesapeake Bay. C. Alabama; Gulf of Mexico. D. Maine; Atlantic Ocean
15. Which eastern capital city is on the Connecticut River?. A. Harrisburg, Pennsylvania. B. Hartford, Connecticut. C. Boston, Massachusetts. D. Providence, Rhode Island
16. Which eastern capital city is on the Susquehanna River?. A. Harrisburg, Pennsylvania. B. Boston, Massachusetts. C. Hartford, Connecticut. D. Providence, Rhode Island
17. Which eastern capital city is on the Atlantic Coast?. A. Boston, Massachusetts. B. Harrisburg, Pennsylvania. C. Providence, Rhode Island. D. Hartford, Connecticut
18. What is the capital city of America’s smallest state and the name of that state?. A. Boston, Massachusetts. B. Harrisburg, Pennsylvania. C. Providence, Rhode Island. D. Hartford, Connecticut
Use the map on p. 104 in the student text NWHG to answer the following questions.
1. What mountain range stopped the American settlers from exploring farther west in the 1760s?. A. Appalachian Mountains. B. Rocky Mountains. C. Sierra Nevada
2. What famous old city was in Spanish territory?. A. St. Augustine. B. Boston. C. Philadelphia
3. Where were most of the cities and towns of the colonies?. A. In the Rocky Mountains. B. Along the Pacific Coast. C. In New England and the Middle Colonies
4. What bay flows into Virginia and Maryland?. A. San Francisco Bay. B. Chesapeake Bay. C. Hudson Bay
5. Who settled the territory north of the colonies?. A. The Russians. B. The Portuguese. C. The French
